sanskrit: tatas tam akṣobhyabalaṃ laṅkāyāṃ nṛpateś caraḥ suvele rāghavaṃ śaile niviṣṭaṃ pratyavedayan
english: Then the king's spies reported to Rāvaṇa in Laṅkā that Rāghava, with his irresistible army, had encamped on the Suvela mountain.

sanskrit: cārāṇāṃ rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptaṃ rāmaṃ mahābalam jātodvego 'bhavat kiṃ cit sacivāṃś cedam abravīt
english: Hearing from the spies that mighty Rāma had arrived, Rāvaṇa became somewhat agitated and spoke thus to his ministers.

sanskrit: mantriṇaḥ śīghram āyāntu sarve vai susamāhitāḥ ayaṃ no mantrakālo hi saṃprāpta iva rākṣasāḥ
english: "Let all the ministers come quickly, fully composed — for this moment of counsel has now arrived for us, O Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tasya tac chāsanaṃ śrutvā mantriṇo 'bhyāgaman drutam tataḥ saṃmantrayām āsa sacivai rākṣasaiḥ saha
english: Hearing that command of his, the ministers came swiftly; then he deliberated together with his Rākṣasa councillors.

sanskrit: mantrayitvā sa durdharṣaḥ kṣamaṃ yat samanantaram visarjayitvā sacivān praviveśa svam ālayam
english: That unconquerable one, having deliberated and resolved upon what was appropriate, dismissed his ministers and entered his own palace.

sanskrit: tato rākṣasam āhūya vidyujjihvaṃ mahābalam māyāvidaṃ mahāmāyaḥ prāviśad yatra maithilī
english: Then that great master of illusion, summoning the mighty Rākṣasa Vidyujjihvā, who was skilled in māyā, entered where Maithilī dwelt.

sanskrit: vidyujjihvaṃ ca māyājñam abravīd rākṣasādhipaḥ mohayiṣyāmahe sītāṃ māyayā janakātmajām
english: The lord of Rākṣasas spoke to Vidyujjihvā, who was versed in illusion: "We shall bewilder Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, through māyā."

sanskrit: śiro māyāmayaṃ gṛhya rāghavasya niśācara māṃ tvaṃ samupatiṣṭhasva mahac ca saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
english: "Taking a head fashioned of illusion belonging to Rāghava, O night-wanderer, present yourself before me, along with a great bow fitted with an arrow."

sanskrit: evam uktas tathety āha vidyujjihvo niśācaraḥ tasya tuṣṭo 'bhavad rājā pradadau ca vibhūṣaṇam
english: So addressed, the night-wanderer Vidyujjihvā said "So be it." The king was pleased with him and bestowed upon him an ornament.

sanskrit: aśokavanikāyāṃ tu praviveśa mahābalaḥ tato dīnām adainyārhāṃ dadarśa dhanadānujaḥ adhomukhīṃ śokaparām upaviṣṭāṃ mahītale
english: That mighty one — the younger brother of Kubera — entered the Aśoka grove and there beheld her who was afflicted though undeserving of affliction, head bowed, overwhelmed by grief, seated on the ground.

sanskrit: bhartāram eva dhyāyantīm aśokavanikāṃ gatām upāsyamānāṃ ghorābhī rākṣasībhir adūrataḥ
english: She was meditating only upon her husband, having come to be in the Aśoka grove, and was being attended upon by terrible Rākṣasī women not far away.

sanskrit: upasṛtya tataḥ sītāṃ praharṣan nāma kīrtayan idaṃ ca vacanaṃ dhṛṣṭam uvāca janakātmajām
english: Approaching Sītā then, proclaiming his joy by name, he spoke this bold speech to the daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: sāntvyamānā mayā bhadre yam upāśritya valgase khara hantā sa te bhartā rāghavaḥ samare hataḥ
english: "While I was comforting you, O fair one, he upon whom you relied and exulted — Rāghava, the slayer of Khara, your husband — has been slain in battle."

sanskrit: chinnaṃ te sarvato mūlaṃ darpas te nihato mayā vyasanenātmanaḥ sīte mama bhāryā bhaviṣyasi
english: "Your root has been cut off on every side; your pride has been destroyed by me. Through my own supremacy, O Sītā, you shall become my wife."

sanskrit: alpapuṇye nivṛttārthe mūḍhe paṇḍitamānini śṛṇu bhartṛbadhaṃ sīte ghoraṃ vṛtravadhaṃ yathā
english: "O woman of little merit, whose purpose is thwarted, foolish one who fancies herself wise — hear, O Sītā, of your husband's slaughter, dreadful as the slaying of Vṛtra."

sanskrit: samāyātaḥ samudrāntaṃ māṃ hantuṃ kila rāghavaḥ vānarendrapraṇītena balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
english: "Rāghava had indeed come to the ocean's edge to slay me, accompanied by a great army led by the king of monkeys."

sanskrit: saṃniviṣṭaḥ samudrasya tīram āsādya dakṣiṇam balena mahatā rāmo vrajaty astaṃ divākare
english: "Rāma, having encamped with his great army on the southern shore of the ocean, was there as the sun went to its setting."

sanskrit: athādhvani pariśrāntam ardharātre sthitaṃ balam sukhasuptaṃ samāsādya cāritaṃ prathamaṃ caraiḥ
english: "Then at midnight, with the army weary from the march and sleeping in ease — this was first reconnoitered by spies —"

sanskrit: tat prahastapraṇītena balena mahatā mama balam asya hataṃ rātrau yatra rāmaḥ sulakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "— my great army, led by Prahasta, slaughtered his army at night, there where Rāma was along with Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: paṭṭasān parighān khaḍgāṃś cakrān daṇḍān mahāyasān bāṇajālāni śūlāni bhāsvarān kūṭamudgarān
english: "Broad-bladed swords, iron clubs, scimitars, discuses, great iron maces, volleys of arrows, spears, gleaming hammers —"

sanskrit: yaṣṭīś ca tomarān prāsaṃś cakrāṇi musalāni ca udyamyodyamya rakṣobhir vānareṣu nipātitāḥ
english: "— staves, javelins, lances, discuses, and pestles — these were raised again and again by the Rākṣasas and hurled upon the monkeys."

sanskrit: atha suptasya rāmasya prahastena pramāthinaḥ asaktaṃ kṛtahastena śiraś chinnaṃ mahāsinā
english: "Then the crushing Prahasta, with a swift and practiced hand, severed with a great sword the head of Rāma while he slept."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇaḥ samutpatya nigṛhīto yadṛcchayā diśaḥ pravrājitaḥ sarvair lakṣmaṇaḥ plavagaiḥ saha
english: "Vibhīṣaṇa, leaping up, was seized by chance and driven away in all directions; and Lakṣmaṇa was expelled along with all the monkeys."

sanskrit: sugrīvo grīvayā śete bhagnayā plavagādhipaḥ nirastahanukaḥ śete hanūmān rākṣasair hataḥ
english: "Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, lies with his neck broken; Hanūmān lies with his jaw knocked out, slain by the Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: jāmbavān atha jānubhyām utpatan nihato yudhi paṭṭasair bahubhiś chinno nikṛttaḥ pādapo yathā
english: "Jāmbavān, having leaped up upon his knees, was struck down in battle, cut to pieces by many broad swords, felled like a tree."

sanskrit: maindaś ca dvividaś cobhau nihatau vānararṣabhau niḥśvasantau rudantau ca rudhireṇa samukṣitau
english: "Both Mainda and Dvivida, those two bull-monkeys, have been slain, gasping and wailing, drenched in blood."

sanskrit: asinābhyāhataś chinno madhye ripuniṣūdanaḥ abhiṣṭanati medinyāṃ panasaḥ panaso yathā
english: "Panasa, that destroyer of foes, struck by a sword and cut in two at the middle, groans upon the earth like a breadfruit tree."

sanskrit: nārācair bahubhiś chinnaḥ śete daryāṃ darīmukhaḥ kumudas tu mahātejā niṣkūjan sāyakair hataḥ
english: "Darīmukha lies in a cave, cut through by many iron arrows; the mighty Kumuda lies crying out, struck by shafts."

sanskrit: aṅgado bahubhiś chinnaḥ śarair āsādya rākṣasaiḥ pātito rudhirodgārī kṣitau nipatito 'ṅgadaḥ
english: "Aṅgada, assailed by the Rākṣasas, cut through by many arrows, has been felled — Aṅgada has fallen to the ground vomiting blood."

sanskrit: harayo mathitā nāgai rathajālais tathāpare śāyitā mṛditās tatra vāyuvegair ivāmbudāḥ
english: "Some monkeys were crushed by elephants, others laid low and trampled by a mass of chariots there, like storm clouds by the force of wind."

sanskrit: pradrutāś ca pare trastā hanyamānā jaghanyataḥ abhidrutās tu rakṣobhiḥ siṃhair iva mahādvipāḥ
english: "Others fled in terror, struck down from behind, pursued by the Rākṣasas like great elephants by lions."

sanskrit: sāgare patitāḥ ke cit ke cid gaganam āśritāḥ ṛkṣā vṛkṣān upārūḍhā vānarais tu vimiśritāḥ
english: "Some fell into the ocean, some took refuge in the sky; the bears climbed trees, mixed together with the monkeys."

sanskrit: sāgarasya ca tīreṣu śaileṣu ca vaneṣu ca piṅgākṣās te virūpākṣair bahubhir bahavo hatāḥ
english: "On the shores of the ocean, on the mountains, and in the forests, many of those tawny-eyed ones were slain by the many misshapen-eyed Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: evaṃ tava hato bhartā sasainyo mama senayā kṣatajārdraṃ rajodhvastam idaṃ cāsyāhṛtaṃ śiraḥ
english: "Thus your husband along with his army has been slain by my army; and this — his head, wet with blood and covered with dust — has been brought here."

sanskrit: tataḥ paramadurdharṣo rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ sītāyām upaśṛṇvantyāṃ rākṣasīm idam abravīt
english: Then Rāvaṇa, most unconquerable lord of the Rākṣasas, while Sītā was listening, spoke thus to a Rākṣasī.

sanskrit: rākṣasaṃ krūrakarmāṇaṃ vidyujjihvaṃ tvam ānaya yena tad rāghavaśiraḥ saṃgrāmāt svayam āhṛtam
english: "Bring to me the Rākṣasa Vidyujjihvā, cruel in his deeds, the one by whom that head of Rāghava was personally brought from the battlefield."

sanskrit: vidyujjihvas tato gṛhya śiras tat saśarāsanam praṇāmaṃ śirasā kṛtvā rāvaṇasyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ
english: Vidyujjihvā then, taking that head along with the bow and arrows, bowed his own head in salutation and stood before Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tam abravīt tato rājā rāvaṇo rākṣasaṃ sthitam vidyujjihvaṃ mahājihvaṃ samīpaparivartinam
english: Then the king Rāvaṇa spoke to the Rākṣasa who stood near him — Vidyujjihvā of the great tongue, who hovered at his side.

sanskrit: agrataḥ kuru sītāyāḥ śīghraṃ dāśaratheḥ śiraḥ avasthāṃ paścimāṃ bhartuḥ kṛpaṇā sādhu paśyatu
english: "Place quickly before Sītā the head of the son of Daśaratha — let the wretched woman behold well her husband's final state."

sanskrit: evam uktaṃ tu tad rakṣaḥ śiras tat priyadarśanam upanikṣipya sītāyāḥ kṣipram antaradhīyata
english: So commanded, that Rākṣasa set down that fair-looking head before Sītā and swiftly vanished from sight.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaś cāpi cikṣepa bhāsvaraṃ kārmukaṃ mahat triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ sītām idam uvāca ha
english: Rāvaṇa also flung down a great gleaming bow famous throughout the three worlds, and spoke thus to Sītā.

sanskrit: idaṃ tat tava rāmasya kārmukaṃ jyāsamanvitam iha prahastenānītaṃ hatvā taṃ niśi mānuṣam
english: "This is that bow of your Rāma, along with its bowstring — brought here by Prahasta after slaying that mortal in the night."

sanskrit: sa vidyujjihvena sahaiva tac chiro dhanuś ca bhūmau vinikīrya rāvaṇaḥ videharājasya sutāṃ yaśasvinīṃ tato 'bravīt tāṃ bhava me vaśānugā
english: And Rāvaṇa, having together with Vidyujjihvā strewn that head and bow upon the ground, then spoke to that illustrious daughter of the king of Videha: "Come under my sway."

sanskrit: sā sītā tac chiro dṛṣṭvā tac ca kārmukam uttamam sugrīvapratisaṃsargam ākhyātaṃ ca hanūmatā
english: Sītā, seeing that head and that excellent bow — and the meeting with Sugrīva that had been reported by Hanūmān —

sanskrit: nayane mukhavarṇaṃ ca bhartus tat sadṛśaṃ mukham keśān keśāntadeśaṃ ca taṃ ca cūḍāmaṇiṃ śubham
english: — the eyes, the complexion, and the face resembling her husband's face, the hair and the hairline, and that beautiful crest jewel —

sanskrit: etaiḥ sarvair abhijñānair abhijñāya suduḥkhitā vijagarhe 'tha kaikeyīṃ krośantī kurarī yathā
english: — recognizing these by all these tokens, deeply grief-stricken, she then denounced Kaikeyī, crying out like an osprey.

sanskrit: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi hato 'yaṃ kulanandanaḥ kulam utsāditaṃ sarvaṃ tvayā kalahaśīlayā
english: "May you have your wish, O Kaikeyī — this joy of the family has been slain. The entire family has been destroyed by you, O quarrelsome one."

sanskrit: āryeṇa kiṃ nu kaikeyyāḥ kṛtaṃ rāmeṇa vipriyam yad gṛhāc cīravasanas tayā prasthāpito vanam
english: "What wrong indeed had the noble Rāma done to Kaikeyī, that she sent him from home, clad in bark garments, to the forest?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu vaidehī vepamānā tapasvinī jagāma jagatīṃ bālā chinnā tu kadalī yathā
english: Having spoken thus, the trembling, suffering Vaidehī, young as she was, fell to the earth like a plantain tree cut down.

sanskrit: sā muhūrtāt samāśvasya pratilabhya ca cetanām tac chiraḥ samupāghrāya vilalāpāyatekṣaṇā
english: She, having recovered after a moment and regaining her senses, smelled that head and lamented, that large-eyed one.

sanskrit: hā hatāsmi mahābāho vīravratam anuvratā imāṃ te paścimāvasthāṃ gatāsmi vidhavā kṛtā
english: "Alas, I am undone, O mighty-armed one! I who faithfully followed a hero's vow — I have come to this final state of yours, made a widow."

sanskrit: prathamaṃ maraṇaṃ nāryā bhartur vaiguṇyam ucyate suvṛttaḥ sādhuvṛttāyāḥ saṃvṛttas tvaṃ mamāgrataḥ
english: "For a woman, they say, a husband's failing is the first death. You who were so nobly conducted toward one of noble conduct — you have preceded me."

sanskrit: duḥkhād duḥkhaṃ prapannāyā magnāyāḥ śokasāgare yo hi mām udyatas trātuṃ so 'pi tvaṃ vinipātitaḥ
english: "For me, who was plunged from sorrow into sorrow, submerged in an ocean of grief — even you who had set out to rescue me have been struck down."

sanskrit: sā śvaśrūr mama kausalyā tvayā putreṇa rāghava vatseneva yathā dhenur vivatsā vatsalā kṛtā
english: "That mother-in-law of mine, Kausalyā, loving as she is, has been made, O Rāghava, bereft of her son by you, like a cow bereft of its calf."

sanskrit: ādiṣṭaṃ dīrgham āyus te yair acintyaparākrama anṛtaṃ vacanaṃ teṣām alpāyur asi rāghava
english: "Those who decreed for you a long life, O you of inconceivable prowess — their words were false; you are short-lived, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: atha vā naśyati prajñā prājñasyāpi satas tava pacaty enaṃ tathā kālo bhūtānāṃ prabhavo hy ayam
english: "Or perhaps even the wisdom of a wise and virtuous person is destroyed — for time, the origin of all beings, cooks them accordingly."

sanskrit: adṛṣṭaṃ mṛtyum āpannaḥ kasmāt tvaṃ nayaśāstravit vyasanānām upāyajñaḥ kuśalo hy asi varjane
english: "How did you meet an unforeseen death, you who were versed in the science of statecraft, skilled in the means of countering adversities, deft at avoiding them?"

sanskrit: tathā tvaṃ saṃpariṣvajya raudrayātinṛśaṃsayā kālarātryā mayācchidya hṛtaḥ kamalalocanaḥ
english: "Thus you, lotus-eyed one, embracing me, were torn away and taken by that savage, utterly cruel night of doom."

sanskrit: upaśeṣe mahābāho māṃ vihāya tapasvinīm priyām iva śubhāṃ nārīṃ pṛthivīṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: "You lie here, O mighty-armed bull among men, having abandoned me, the suffering one — as one abandons the beloved earth, that fair woman."

sanskrit: arcitaṃ satataṃ yatnād gandhamālyair mayā tava idaṃ te matpriyaṃ vīra dhanuḥ kāñcanabhūṣitam
english: "This bow of yours, adorned with gold, beloved of me — O hero, it was always carefully honored by me with fragrant garlands."

sanskrit: pitrā daśarathena tvaṃ śvaśureṇa mamānagha pūrvaiś ca pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ nūnaṃ svarge samāgataḥ
english: "You have surely met in heaven, O sinless one, with your father Daśaratha — my father-in-law — and with your ancestral forebears."

sanskrit: divi nakṣatrabhūtas tvaṃ mahat karma kṛtaṃ priyam puṇyaṃ rājarṣivaṃśaṃ tvam ātmanaḥ samupekṣase
english: "You have become a star in the heavens; great and beloved deeds have been done. You look down upon the holy lineage of royal sages that is your own."

sanskrit: kiṃ mān na prekṣase rājan kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase bālāṃ bālena saṃprāptāṃ bhāryāṃ māṃ sahacāriṇīm
english: "Why do you not look at me, O king? Why do you not speak to me — to me, your wife, your companion, the young one who was joined to you in youth?"

sanskrit: saṃśrutaṃ gṛhṇatā pāṇiṃ cariṣyāmīti yat tvayā smara tan mama kākutstha naya mām api duḥkhitām
english: "What you promised while taking my hand — 'I shall go with you' — remember that, O Kākutstha, and take me too, who am in such distress."

sanskrit: kasmān mām apahāya tvaṃ gato gatimatāṃ vara asmāl lokād amuṃ lokaṃ tyaktvā mām iha duḥkhitām
english: "Why have you gone, abandoning me, O best among those who move — from this world to that other world, leaving me here in sorrow?"

sanskrit: kalyāṇair ucitaṃ yat tat pariṣvaktaṃ mayaiva tu kravyādais tac charīraṃ te nūnaṃ viparikṛṣyate
english: "That body of yours, worthy of all auspicious things, embraced by me alone — that body is surely now being torn apart by flesh-eaters."

sanskrit: agniṣṭomādibhir yajñair iṣṭavān āptadakṣiṇaiḥ agnihotreṇa saṃskāraṃ kena tvaṃ tu na lapsyase
english: "You who had performed sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma and others, with proper dakṣiṇā given — why shall you not obtain the proper rites of the Agnihotra?"

sanskrit: pravrajyām upapannānāṃ trayāṇām ekam āgatam pariprakṣyati kausalyā lakṣmaṇaṃ śokalālasā
english: "Kausalyā, frantic with grief, will question Lakṣmaṇa, the one who has come back of the three who set out into the forest."

sanskrit: sa tasyāḥ paripṛcchantyā vadhaṃ mitrabalasya te tava cākhyāsyate nūnaṃ niśāyāṃ rākṣasair vadham
english: "To her who questions, he will surely tell of the slaughter of Mitra and Bala, and of your slaughter by the Rākṣasas in the night."

sanskrit: sā tvāṃ suptaṃ hataṃ śrutvā māṃ ca rakṣogṛhaṃ gatām hṛdayena vidīrṇena na bhaviṣyati rāghava
english: "Hearing that you were slain while asleep, and that I have gone to the Rākṣasa's house — she will be no more, O Rāghava, her heart burst asunder."

sanskrit: sādhu pātaya māṃ kṣipraṃ rāmasyopari rāvaṇaḥ samānaya patiṃ patnyā kuru kalyāṇam uttamam
english: "Do well, O Rāvaṇa — cast me quickly upon Rāma; unite wife with husband — do the highest good."

sanskrit: śirasā me śiraś cāsya kāyaṃ kāyena yojaya rāvaṇānugamiṣyāmi gatiṃ bhartur mahātmanaḥ muhūrtam api necchāmi jīvituṃ pāpajīvinā
english: "Join my head to his head, my body to his body. I will follow, after Rāvaṇa, the course of my noble husband — I do not wish to live even a moment more with this sinful life."

sanskrit: śrutaṃ mayā vedavidāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ pitur gṛhe yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ priyo bhartā tāsāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ
english: "I heard in my father's house from Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas: those women whose husband is dear to them — for those women the worlds are of great glory."

sanskrit: kṣamā yasmin damas tyāgaḥ satyaṃ dharmaḥ kṛtajñatā ahiṃsā caiva bhūtānāṃ tam ṛte kā gatir mama
english: "In whom forgiveness, self-restraint, generosity, truth, righteousness, gratitude, and non-injury toward all beings resided — without him, what course is there for me?"

sanskrit: iti sā duḥkhasaṃtaptā vilalāpāyatekṣaṇā bhartuḥ śiro dhanus tatra samīkṣya janakātmajā
english: Thus the large-eyed daughter of Janaka, scorched by grief, lamented there, gazing upon her husband's head and bow.

sanskrit: evaṃ lālapyamānāyāṃ sītāyāṃ tatra rākṣasaḥ abhicakrāma bhartāram anīkasthaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: While Sītā was lamenting thus, a Rākṣasa who stood in the ranks approached his master there with hands cupped in reverence.

sanskrit: vijayasvāryaputreti so 'bhivādya prasādya ca nyavedayad anuprāptaṃ prahastaṃ vāhinīpatim
english: Saluting and propitiating him with "Be victorious, O son of a noble," he announced that Prahasta, the commander of the army, had arrived.

sanskrit: amātyaiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ prahastaḥ samupasthitaḥ kiṃ cid ātyayikaṃ kāryaṃ teṣāṃ tvaṃ darśanaṃ kuru
english: "Prahasta has come with all the ministers. There is some urgent matter — grant them an audience."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā daśagrīvo rākṣasaprativeditam aśokavanikāṃ tyaktvā mantriṇāṃ darśanaṃ yayau
english: Hearing this, reported by the Rākṣasa, the ten-necked one left the Aśoka grove and went to give audience to the ministers.

sanskrit: sa tu sarvaṃ samarthyaiva mantribhiḥ kṛtyam ātmanaḥ sabhāṃ praviśya vidadhe viditvā rāmavikramam
english: He, having fully deliberated upon all his own duties with the ministers, entered the assembly hall and made his arrangements, knowing well Rāma's prowess.

sanskrit: antardhānaṃ tu tac chīrṣaṃ tac ca kārmukam uttamam jagāma rāvaṇasyaiva niryāṇasamanantaram
english: That head and that excellent bow vanished into invisibility immediately upon Rāvaṇa's departure.

sanskrit: rākṣasendras tu taiḥ sārdhaṃ mantribhir bhīmavikramaiḥ samarthayām āsa tadā rāmakāryaviniścayam
english: The lord of the Rākṣasas, together with those ministers of fearsome prowess, then deliberated upon and resolved the matter of what was to be done about Rāma.

sanskrit: avidūrasthitān sarvān balādhyakṣān hitaiṣiṇaḥ abravīt kālasadṛśo rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas, resembling Death itself, spoke to all the commanders of the army who stood not far away, those who sought his welfare.

sanskrit: śīghraṃ bherīninādena sphuṭakoṇāhatena me samānayadhvaṃ sainyāni vaktavyaṃ ca na kāraṇam
english: "Swiftly, with the resounding beat of drums struck on their corners, muster my armies — no reason need be given."

sanskrit: tatas tatheti pratigṛhya tad vaco balādhipās te mahad ātmano balam samānayaṃś caiva samāgataṃ ca te nyavedayan bhartari yuddhakāṅkṣiṇi
english: Then those army commanders, accepting his word with "So be it," mustered their own great forces and reported to their lord — he who was eager for battle — that they had assembled.

sanskrit: sītāṃ tu mohitāṃ dṛṣṭvā saramā nāma rākṣasī āsasādāśu vaidehīṃ priyāṃ praṇayinī sakhī
english: Seeing Sītā bewildered, a Rākṣasī named Saramā — a dear and affectionate friend — quickly approached Vaidehī.

sanskrit: sā hi tatra kṛtā mitraṃ sītayā rakṣyamāṇayā rakṣantī rāvaṇād iṣṭā sānukrośā dṛḍhavratā
english: She had there been made a friend by Sītā even while Sītā was being guarded; she was beloved by Rāvaṇa, yet she protected Sītā, compassionate and firm in her purpose.

sanskrit: sā dadarśa sakhīṃ sītāṃ saramā naṣṭacetanām upāvṛtyotthitāṃ dhvastāṃ vaḍavām iva pāṃsuṣu
english: Saramā saw her friend Sītā senseless, having partially risen and then collapsed, like a mare in the dust.

sanskrit: tāṃ samāśvāsayām āsa sakhī snehena suvratā uktā yad rāvaṇena tvaṃ pratyuktaṃ ca svayaṃ tvayā
english: That friend of noble vows comforted her with affection, knowing all that Rāvaṇa had said to her and all that she herself had said in reply.

sanskrit: sakhīsnehena tad bhīru mayā sarvaṃ pratiśrutam līnayā ganahe śūhye bhayam utsṛjya rāvaṇāt tava hetor viśālākṣi na hi me jīvitaṃ priyam
english: "Out of a friend's love, O timid one, I listened to everything, concealed in the dense thicket, casting off fear of Rāvaṇa — for your sake, O large-eyed one, my life is not dear to me."

sanskrit: sa saṃbhrāntaś ca niṣkrānto yat kṛte rākṣasādhipaḥ tac ca me viditaṃ sarvam abhiniṣkramya maithili
english: "And for what reason the lord of Rākṣasas departed in agitation — all that has become known to me upon his departure, O Maithilī."

sanskrit: na śakyaṃ sauptikaṃ kartuṃ rāmasya viditātmanaḥ vadhaś ca puruṣavyāghre tasminn evopapadyate
english: "It is impossible to perform a night attack against Rāma, whose self is known and alert; and indeed the slaughter befits that tiger among men alone."

sanskrit: na caiva vānarā hantuṃ śakyāḥ pādapayodhinaḥ surā devarṣabheṇeva rāmeṇa hi surakṣitāḥ
english: "Nor can the tree-dwelling monkeys be slain — they are well-guarded by Rāma, as the gods are guarded by the bull among gods."

sanskrit: dīrghavṛttabhujaḥ śrīmān mahoraskaḥ pratāpavān dhanvī saṃhananopeto dharmātmā bhuvi viśrutaḥ
english: "Long and rounded of arm, radiant, broad-chested, of great majesty, a bowman endowed with a firm physique, righteous in soul, renowned in the world —"

sanskrit: vikrānto rakṣitā nityam ātmanaś ca parasya ca lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā kuśalī nayaśāstravit
english: "— valiant, ever the protector of himself and others, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, skilled, versed in the science of statecraft —"

sanskrit: hantā parabalaughānām acintyabalapauruṣaḥ na hato rāghavaḥ śrīmān sīte śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
english: "— destroyer of enemy hosts, of inconceivable strength and valor — glorious Rāghava, the crusher of foes, has not been slain, O Sītā."

sanskrit: ayuktabuddhikṛtyena sarvabhūtavirodhinā iyaṃ prayuktā raudreṇa māyā māyāvidā tvayi
english: "This māyā has been deployed against you by that savage who is skilled in illusion, whose acts of mind are crooked, who is hostile to all beings."

sanskrit: śokas te vigataḥ sarvaḥ kalyāṇaṃ tvām upasthitam dhruvaṃ tvāṃ bhajate lakṣmīḥ priyaṃ prītikaraṃ śṛṇu
english: "All your grief has departed; good fortune stands before you. Prosperity surely attends you — hear something dear and joyful."

sanskrit: uttīrya sāgaraṃ rāmaḥ saha vānarasenayā saṃniviṣṭaḥ samudrasya tīram āsādya dakṣiṇam
english: "Rāma, having crossed the ocean with his army of monkeys, has encamped having reached the southern shore of the sea."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭo me paripūrṇārthaḥ kākutsthaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ sahitaiḥ sāgarāntasthair balais tiṣṭhati rakṣitaḥ
english: "I have seen Kākutstha, his purpose fully accomplished, together with Lakṣmaṇa, standing guarded, his forces arrayed at the ocean's edge."

sanskrit: anena preṣitā ye ca rākṣasā laghuvikramaḥ rāghavas tīrṇa ity evaṃ pravṛttis tair ihāhṛtā
english: "And the Rākṣasas sent out by Rāvaṇa — those swift ones — have brought back this intelligence: that Rāghava has crossed over."

sanskrit: sa tāṃ śrutvā viśālākṣi pravṛttiṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ eṣa mantrayate sarvaiḥ sacivaiḥ saha rāvaṇaḥ
english: "Having heard that intelligence, O large-eyed one, the lord of the Rākṣasas — this Rāvaṇa — is now deliberating with all his ministers."

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇā saramā rākṣasī sītayā saha sarvodyogena sainyānāṃ śabdaṃ śuśrāva bhairavam
english: As the Rākṣasī Saramā was speaking thus with Sītā, they heard the dreadful sound of armies in full mobilization.

sanskrit: daṇḍanirghātavādinyāḥ śrutvā bheryā mahāsvanam uvāca saramā sītām idaṃ madhurabhāṣiṇī
english: Hearing the great sound of the drum struck by the drum-stick, the sweet-speaking Saramā said this to Sītā.

sanskrit: saṃnāhajananī hy eṣā bhairavā bhīru bherikā bherīnādaṃ ca gambhīraṃ śṛṇu toyadanisvanam
english: "This dread drum that calls men to armor — O timid one, hear the deep resonance of the drum, like the thunder of rain-clouds."

sanskrit: kalpyante mattamātaṃgā yujyante rathavājinaḥ tatra tatra ca saṃnaddhāḥ saṃpatanti padātayaḥ
english: "Raging war-elephants are being harnessed, chariot-horses are being yoked; here and there armored infantry come rushing."

sanskrit: āpūryante rājamārgāḥ sainyair adbhutadarśanaiḥ vegavadbhir nadadbhiś ca toyaughair iva sāgaraḥ
english: "The royal highways are filling with armies of wondrous appearance, swift and thundering, as the ocean fills with torrents of water."

sanskrit: śāstrāṇāṃ ca prasannānāṃ carmaṇāṃ varmaṇāṃ tathā rathavājigajānāṃ ca bhūṣitānāṃ ca rakṣasām
english: "Of polished weapons, shields, and coats of mail, of chariots, horses, and elephants, and of the adorned Rākṣasas —"

sanskrit: prabhāṃ visṛjatāṃ paśya nānāvarṇāṃ samutthitām vanaṃ nirdahato dharme yathārūpaṃ vibhāvasoḥ
english: "— behold the radiance of many colors rising up, like that of fire in its proper form when it burns a forest."

sanskrit: ghaṇṭānāṃ śṛṇu nirghoṣaṃ rathānāṃ śṛṇu nisvanam hayānāṃ heṣamāṇānāṃ śṛṇu tūryadhvaniṃ yathā
english: "Hear the clanging of bells, hear the rumble of chariots, hear the neighing of horses and the sound of martial instruments."

sanskrit: udyatāyudhahastānāṃ rākṣasendrānuyāyinām saṃbhramo rakṣasām eṣa tumulo lomaharṣaṇaḥ
english: "This tumultuous, hair-raising commotion is that of the Rākṣasas, weapons raised in hand, following in the train of the lord of Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: śrīs tvāṃ bhajati śokaghnī rakṣasāṃ bhayam āgatam rāmāt kamalapatrākṣi daityānām iva vāsavāt
english: "Prosperity, the destroyer of grief, attends you; fear has come upon the Rākṣasas from Rāma, O lotus-petal-eyed one, as fear came upon the Daityas from Vāsava."

sanskrit: avajitya jitakrodhas tam acintyaparākramaḥ rāvaṇaṃ samare hatvā bhartā tvādhigamiṣyati
english: "Conquering him, having mastered his wrath, that one of inconceivable prowess — your husband — will slay Rāvaṇa in battle and come to you."

sanskrit: vikramiṣyati rakṣaḥsu bhartā te sahalakṣmaṇaḥ yathā śatruṣu śatrughno viṣṇunā saha vāsavaḥ
english: "Your husband, together with Lakṣmaṇa, will wage valiant war against the Rākṣasas, as Vāsava together with Viṣṇu wages war against his enemies."

sanskrit: āgatasya hi rāmasya kṣipram aṅkagatāṃ satīm ahaṃ drakṣyāmi siddhārthāṃ tvāṃ śatrau vinipātite
english: "When Rāma has arrived and the enemy has been laid low, I shall quickly see you — virtuous one, your purpose achieved — held in his embrace."

sanskrit: aśrūṇy ānandajāni tvaṃ vartayiṣyasi śobhane samāgamya pariṣvaktā tasyorasi mahorasaḥ
english: "You, O beautiful one, will shed tears born of joy, having met and been embraced upon the broad chest of that broad-chested one."

sanskrit: acirān mokṣyate sīte devi te jaghanaṃ gatām dhṛtām etāṃ bahūn māsān veṇīṃ rāmo mahābalaḥ
english: "Before long, O Sītā, O queen, mighty Rāma will free this braid that has fallen to your hips, kept these many months."

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ devi pūrṇacandram ivoditam mokṣyase śokajaṃ vāri nirmokam iva pannagī
english: "Seeing his face, O queen, risen like the full moon, you will shed the water born of grief, as a serpent sheds its slough."

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ samare hatvā nacirād eva maithili tvayā samagraṃ priyayā sukhārho lapsyate sukham
english: "Having slain Rāvaṇa in battle before long, O Maithilī, he who deserves happiness will attain happiness, complete, together with you, his beloved."

sanskrit: samāgatā tvaṃ rāmeṇa modiṣyasi mahātmanā suvarṣeṇa samāyuktā yathā sasyena medinī
english: "Reunited with Rāma the great-souled one, you shall rejoice, as the earth rejoices when blessed with good rain and crops."

sanskrit: girivaram abhito 'nuvartamāno haya iva maṇḍalam āśu yaḥ karoti tam iha śaraṇam abhyupehi devi divasakaraṃ prabhavo hy ayaṃ prajānām
english: "He who swiftly circles the best of mountains all around, like a horse making its circuit — seek refuge here, O queen, in that maker of day, for he is the origin of all creatures."
